transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm really struggling with how my face looks, especially my skin. I have this horrible acne and scarring that is just so obvious and ugly, and I can't stop thinking about it. It's honestly taking over my life.
How much time do you spend each day thinking about your skin or checking your appearance in the mirror?

I honestly spend several hours every day obsessing over my skin and constantly checking myself in any mirror I can find. It makes me feel incredibly anxious and self-conscious, but I just feel this overwhelming urge to keep checking for flaws throughout the day. I can't seem to stop.
Do you ever feel that your concerns about your skin are excessive or not completely true, even though you still can't stop thinking about them?

Sometimes I do wonder if I'm overreacting, especially since everyone else tells me my skin looks fine and that my worries are overblown. But even so, I still feel completely consumed by the belief that my acne and scars look terrible, and I just can't get it out of my head.
Do you engage in any repetitive behaviors, like skin picking or excessive grooming, in response to your concerns about your skin?

Yes, I constantly pick at my skin and squeeze the bumps to try and make them go away or look smoother. I do it so much that it probably makes the redness and scarring even worse, but I just can't stop trying to fix it.

These features are hallmark criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder. No other diagnoses from the allowed list better account for the full clinical picture, and no new information contradicts the initial candidate. Therefore, the current candidates remain unchanged.
